title: How Do Image/Video Generation Work?
reading: The slide explains text-to-image/video generation via diffusion models: noise is gradually added to data and the model learns to reverse that process. It states the training data consists of paired inputs (captions) and outputs (images). A pipeline figure below illustrates conditional denoising driven by text embeddings from a frozen text encoder.

visuals.description: Left-to-right pipeline: a pure-noise image passes through a green hourglass-shaped (U-Net-like) denoiser, producing a noisy puppy image, then a second denoiser produces a clean golden puppy photo. Each denoiser receives an upward arrow from a bracketed row of orange text-embedding vectors, both emitted by an orange 'Frozen text encoder' bar fed the caption "A golden lab puppy, tongue hanging out, and wearing a blue collar".
visuals.assertion: Sampling iteratively denoises from Gaussian noise to an image, with each step conditioned on text embeddings produced by a frozen text encoder from the caption.

concepts.name: Diffusion models
concepts.why_it_matters: Core generative mechanism: add Gaussian noise then learn the reverse denoising process.

concepts.name: Frozen text encoder / text embedding
concepts.why_it_matters: Provides the conditioning signal that steers generation toward the caption.

concepts.name: Caption-image training pairs
concepts.why_it_matters: Defines the supervision needed for text-conditioned generation.

verbatim_spans: Diffusion models: Gradually add Gaussian noise and then learn to reverse
